## Regressions

💭 nit  Select's cancel became optional, so a caller compiles without the iOS sheet's cancel action
- key: src/design-system/Select.tsx#cancel-optional
- Where: src/design-system/Select.tsx:14-15 `cancel?: string | undefined` (round 1: `cancel: string`); Select.ios.tsx:18-19 then opens the sheet with no cancel button. The one caller passes it today (src/shell/TopBar.tsx:116).
- Why: my round-1 advice (key src/design-system#api-conventions) made it optional because web and Android ignore it, but every caller is shared code that also runs on iOS, so the type was the only guard. A plan C filter Select that leaves it out opens a sheet the user can leave only by picking an option [Unverified - confirm before applying: an iPhone action sheet with no cancel action is not dismissed by a tap outside].
- Fix: restore `cancel: string` and reword Select.tsx:14 to `// The iOS sheet's cancel button; web and Android ignore it.`
- approach-changing: no, one type annotation

## New findings

🟡 major  Still open: text a model returns, or a component picks by a condition, passes the user-text rule
- key: eslint.config.js#screens-text-guard
- Where: eslint-rules/restrictions.js:31-34 match a string only when it is the direct child of JSX or of a naming prop; eslint.config.js:80 gives model files (src/**/model{,.*}.ts) restricted, animatedText and pureDynamicImports only, no text rule. measured: a probe linted as src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/Probe.tsx flagged 7 of 10 planted texts and passed `{EMPTY}` (a const), `{n > 0 ? 'Some items' : 'None'}` and `label={n > 1 ? 'Open all' : 'Open one'}`; a probe linted as src/screens/24-project-overview/model.probe.ts holding `() => 'No items'`, `a + ', ' + b`, `xs.join(', ')` and a template `${n} items left` exited 0.
- Why: models are where screen 24 assembles every visible sentence (model.ts, model.lists.ts), and plan C copies that shape; a model that returns 'No items' or joins with ', ' ships English text and English punctuation into the vi page with every gate green. CONTRIBUTING.md:73 ("Never build a sentence by concatenation") and :166-169 read as enforced, but the model half is review-only. Today's tree is clean: the round-1 joiners now go through templates (model.ts:52, 104, 127; model.lists.ts:113).
- Fix: (1) in restrictions.js uiText, also match a string under a condition: `:matches(JSXElement, JSXFragment) > JSXExpressionContainer > :matches(ConditionalExpression, LogicalExpression) :matches(Literal[value=/[A-Za-z]/], TemplateLiteral)`, and the same under `${NAMED_BY} > JSXExpressionContainer`; (2) add a list for model files (tests excluded) that rejects a string literal holding a space or punctuation outside `{slot}` names, a `+` with a string operand and a `.join()` call, skipping `ThrowStatement` descendants and import sources. By my reading of model.ts, model.lists.ts and model.tools.ts the only such string today is the error message at model.ts:55, which the throw exemption covers; measure on src/shell/model*.ts before enabling (NOT RUN: not read in this review).
- approach-changing: no, two selector lists in restrictions.js
- trigger: a plan C block writes `label={open ? 'Close' : 'Open'}`, or a model returns `count === 0 ? 'No items' : ...`; the vi page shows English
- guard-bypass: restrictions.js:32 and :34 require the Literal to be the JSXExpressionContainer's direct child, so a ConditionalExpression or an Identifier in between hides it; no block of eslint.config.js gives model files a text list (eslint.config.js:80)
- design: yes, a text rule for model files and for conditional JSX text (neither exists)

🟡 major  The health level look (mark and colour) is defined twice, in the shell's project header and in screen 24's Health card
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/HealthCard.styles.ts#rag-map-twice
- Where: src/shell/ProjectHeader.tsx:15-19 `RAG = { green: { glyph: 'ragGreen', tone: 'good' }, amber: { glyph: 'ragAmber', tone: 'waiting' }, red: { glyph: 'ragRed', tone: 'critical' } }` and src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/HealthCard.styles.ts:11-16 `levelMarks`, the same three entries plus unknown. Both draw a RAG level on screen 24: the header above the body (Screen.tsx:51) and the Health card's two lines (HealthCard.tsx:36-37). measured: `rtk proxy grep -rn "ragGreen\|ragAmber" src` minus tests: two maps, plus Glyph.tsx's glyph table.
- Why: CONTRIBUTING.md:55 says each value is defined once; a designer who retunes amber (its glyph or tone) in one map makes one health level look different in the header and in the card on the same page, and BR-39 (shape and words, never colour alone) relies on one set of marks. Screens may not import each other (eslint.config.js:147-153), so every plan C screen that shows a RAG level (portfolio, program, steering committee) adds another copy.
- Fix: move the map into the design system beside STATUS, for example `src/design-system/health.ts` exporting `HEALTH_MARK: Record<'green' | 'amber' | 'red' | 'unknown', { glyph: GlyphName; tone: GlyphTone }>` (or a `HealthMark` component that draws the Glyph), import it in ProjectHeader.tsx and HealthCard.tsx, and pin it in one test.
- approach-changing: no, one shared table
- trigger: amber moves to the serious tone in HealthCard.styles.ts:13 only; at desktop width the header and the card show the same level in two colours
- guard-bypass: each map is pinned at most by its own component's tests (the grep finds levelMarks in HealthCard.test.native.tsx and no shell test naming RAG); nothing compares the two, and the restated-literal rule reads test files only (eslint.config.js:72-74)

💭 nit  Still open: unitless style values sit outside the token rule, while CONTRIBUTING says every literal number is rejected
- key: eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js#gaps
- Where: eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js:2-3 (SIZED) and :66 skip any key not in that list; CONTRIBUTING.md:161-163 says "a literal number or colour in a style is rejected unless the line above says // token-exception". The tree keeps src/design-system/Select.styles.ts:39 `opacity: 0.01` and src/design-system/Menu.styles.ts:12 `zIndex: 1` with no marker. measured: a probe linted as src/design-system/Probe.styles.ts flagged 12 values (const, call, px, arithmetic, colours) and passed `opacity: 0.5`, `opacity: HALF` (a const), `zIndex: 3`, `aspectRatio: 1.5` and `shadowOpacity: 0.3`.
- Why: the 0.01 opacity is a measured Android workaround (Select.styles.ts:38) that a later tidy-up can set to 0 with no marker saying the value is deliberate; the written rule promises a check that does not run, so reviewers skip it.
- Fix: add `opacity|zIndex|aspectRatio|shadowOpacity` to the rule as "a token or a token-exception" (flexGrow stays out: Meter.styles.ts:20-21, ShareBar.styles.ts:13-14 and StackBar.styles.ts:17 compute it from data), then put `// token-exception: TalkBack and Maestro skip a view at opacity 0` above Select.styles.ts:39 and a reason above Menu.styles.ts:12; or reword CONTRIBUTING.md:161 to "a literal size or colour" and name the keys left to review.
- approach-changing: no, rule cases or one sentence

💭 nit  Still open in the gate: an English date or a section reference in a comment passes check-language
- key: src/design-system+src/screens#reference-comments
- Where: CONTRIBUTING.md:21 says check-language checks "the banned references under Comments", and CONTRIBUTING.md:30-31 bans "spec section numbers, line numbers of a reference file, dates, measurement logs". measured: `node scripts/check-language.mjs <probe>` on a 15-line probe reported 9 problems on 8 lines (Vietnamese, R-B15, spec 4.4, wireframe.css:199, Task 9, D-B14, FE-23, spec section 7.2, css:85) and passed `// measured on 9 Oct 2026`, `// per section 4.4 of the spec`, `// see §4.4`, `/* plan C will add this */` and `// wireframes/screens/24-project-overview.html line 120`.
- Why: round 1 counted 7 dated measurement logs in this scope; they were Vietnamese, so non-ascii-letter caught them, but the same log written in English passes, and the next maintainer gets "measured on 9 Oct" with no fact behind it.
- Fix: in scripts/check-language.mjs, inside comments only, reject `\b\d{1,2} (Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]* \d{4}\b`, `\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b`, `§\s*\d`, `\bsection \d+(\.\d+)*`, `\bplan [A-Z]\b` and `\.(html|css|md) line \d+`, each with one probe line in the script's test.
- approach-changing: no, patterns in an existing gate

💭 nit  On iOS and Android a long PIC name can run out of the workload label cell, the one text-beside-a-mark row left without a shrink wrapper
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/WorkloadCard.tsx#name-no-shrink
- Where: WorkloadCard.tsx:25-33 puts a 24 px Avatar and the name Text in a Row inside BarRow's fixed label cell (BarRow.tsx:25, BarRow.styles.ts:8 `width: tokens.barLabelW`, 120 px; gap space10), leaving 86 px for the name. The repo's own measured note says "Native text does not shrink in a row as web text does" (ProgressCard.styles.ts:7) and fixes it in ProgressCard.tsx:23 (a flexShrink 1 View) and ListRow.styles.ts:25-26 (`flex: 1, minWidth: 0`); the workload row has neither. Not a regression: round 1's `person` style was the same row.
- Why: names now come from the server (src/core/api/overview.ts:78); a Vietnamese full name such as "Nguyen Thi Minh Khai" in the small variant is wider than 86 px, so it would draw over the bar [Unverified - confirm before applying on the iPhone 18 Pro simulator with a 20-letter PIC name; NOT RUN: the brief forbids simulators during this review]. Every fixture PIC is of the "Denny K." form (src/mocks/fixtures/meridian.ts), so no test or screenshot shows it, and the web narrow gate cannot, since web text shrinks.
- Fix: wrap the name as ProgressCard does, `<View style={styles.name}><Text variant="small">{row.name}</Text></View>` with `name: { flexShrink: 1 }` in a WorkloadCard.styles.ts, or give Row a shrink option for its last child so plan C rows get it once.
- approach-changing: no, one wrapper

💭 nit  CONTRIBUTING and the lint config describe an Animated.Text in Text.tsx that does not exist
- key: eslint.config.js#animated-text-exemption
- Where: CONTRIBUTING.md:195-196 "only `Text.tsx` draws `Animated.Text`", eslint.config.js:76 (comment) and :79 (Text.tsx gets its list without animatedText); src/design-system/Text.tsx:2 imports the plain `Text as NativeText` and draws it at :48. measured: `rtk proxy grep -rn Animated src` minus tests printed 0 lines.
- Why: the exemption lets Text.tsx add an Animated.Text with no lint error, and the sentence tells plan C developers something false about the one component every text goes through.
- Fix: delete eslint.config.js:79 so Text.tsx keeps line 78's full list (its only JSX child is `{children}`, which uiText does not match), drop the clause from CONTRIBUTING.md:195-196 and the comment at eslint.config.js:76, and update eslint-rules/config.test.js if it pins the exemption (not read).
- approach-changing: no, one config line and one sentence
